ambiguities: Mme de Villeparisis and duc de Guermantes appear only in Saint-Loup's genealogical exposition (the duchesse is Mme de Villeparisis's niece, raised by her, and married her cousin the current duc de Guermantes); this is factual family history with no local praise, blame, or status shift directed at either of them.
prince des Laumes is named only as a superseded title that Charlus's brother (the current duc de Guermantes) held before inheriting the duchy; it is not a distinct evaluative event.

Odette and Gilberte appear only in the closing sentence, as part of the narrator's recollection that Charlus's hard stare matched one seen 'au moment où Odette avait appelé Gilberte' at Tansonville; this is a temporal/referential anchor for Charlus's gaze, not a local appraisal of either woman.

Le narrateur functions as questioner and listener in the dialogue, and as the object of the hard look he now recognizes as Charlus's; this is perceptual/recollective recognition rather than a staged social outcome (inclusion/exclusion, deference, or leverage shift) landing on him as a participant, so no event was scored.
